title: On the Prospects of Dynamic LLM Conversations in Software Development
abstract: arXiv:2608.30756v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become an essential tool for assisting developers, yet we still lack knowledge on ways to effectively support their interactions during development activities. That is, the quality of interactions with a chat-based LLM still strongly depends on how developers phrase prompts and which information they include.   Our goal is to evaluate whether interventions into these interactions with LLMs have an effect on software developers---be it harmful or beneficial. To this end, we conducted a four-month longitudinal study with third-semester computer science students working on a full-stack Web development project using chat-based LLMs under three conditions: (1) a \emph{context}-aware group received intent-based conversation augmentation, (2) a \emph{proactive} group received follow-up suggestions and tailored advice, and (3) a \emph{control} group without intervention. translated_title: 论软件开发中动态大语言模型对话的前景
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已成为辅助开发者的重要工具，但我们仍缺乏关于如何在开发活动中有效支持人机交互的知识。也就是说，与基于聊天的LLM交互的质量在很大程度上取决于开发者如何表述提示词以及他们在提示中包含哪些信息。我们的目标是评估对开发者与LLM的这些交互进行干预是否会对软件开发者产生影响——无论是有害的还是有益的。为此，我们对第三学期的计算机科学学生开展了一项为期四个月的纵向研究，这些学生在全栈Web开发项目中使用基于聊天的LLM，并分为三种条件：（1）*情境感知*组接受基于意图的对话增强；（2）*主动*组接受后续建议和量身定制的指导；（3）*对照组*不接受任何干预。我们的增强措施非常精简：（i）……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究通过为期四个月的纵向实验发现，对开发者与LLM的对话进行情境感知或主动式建议等最小化干预能够对软件开发者产生实际影响，为动态LLM对话在软件开发中的应用前景提供了实证依据。
